[[Image:Aspidistra flower.jpg|thumb|Flower]]
'''''Aspidistra elatior''''', the '''cast-iron-plant'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''bar-room plant''', also known in [[Japanese language|Japanese]] as ''haran'' or ''baran'' (葉蘭)<ref>{{GRIN | accessdate = 4 January 2018}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asparagaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to [[Japan]] and [[Taiwan]]. Tolerant of neglect, it is widely cultivated as a [[houseplant]], but can also be grown outside in shade where temperatures remain above {{convert|-15|C|F|0}}. It is used as training material for the ''[[seika]]'' form of ''[[ikebana]]''.

==Description==
Growing to {{convert|60|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall and wide, it is an [[evergreen]] [[rhizomatous]] perennial, with glossy dark-green leaves {{convert|30|-|50|cm|0|abbr=on}} long and fleshy 8-lobed cream flowers with maroon colouring on the inner surface borne in early summer.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

== Pollination ==
According to a study published in 2018, ''A. elatior'' appears to be mainly pollinated by [[Fungus gnat|fungus gnats]] (''[[Cordyla sixi]]'' and ''[[Bradysia]]'' spp.'')''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Suetsugu|first1=Kenji|last2=Sueyoshi|first2=Masahiro|date=2018-01-01|title=Subterranean flowers of ''Aspidistra elatior'' are mainly pollinated by not terrestrial amphipods but fungus gnats|journal=Ecology|volume=99|issue=1|pages=244–246|doi=10.1002/ecy.2021|pmid=29136275|bibcode=2018Ecol...99..244S |issn=1939-9170|url=http://www.lib.kobe-u.ac.jp/repository/90004538.pdf}}</ref>

==Distribution==
Although sometimes thought to be of Chinese origin,<ref name=FOC>{{cite web|title=Aspidistra elatior|work=Flora of China| url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200027584|accessdate=2009-02-19}}</ref> the species is in fact native to southern Japan,<ref name=WCSP_275646>{{Cite web |title=''Aspidistra elator''|work=World Checklist of Selected Plant Families |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] |url=http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=275646 |accessdate=2013-07-22}}</ref> including [[Kuroshima (Kagoshima)|Kuroshima]],<ref name=kuroshima>{{cite journal |last=Sako |first=Shizuo |author2=Katsutoshi Maruno |date=March 1983 |title=Flora of Island Kuroshima, Pref. Kagoshima, Kyushu |journal=Bulletin of the Kagoshima University Forest |volume=11 |pages=33–61 |issn=0389-9454 |url=http://ir.kagoshima-u.ac.jp/bitstream/10232/945/1/KJ00000067228.pdf |accessdate=2009-02-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718170351/http://ir.kagoshima-u.ac.jp/bitstream/10232/945/1/KJ00000067228.pdf |archive-date=2011-07-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Suwanosejima]]<ref name=suwanose>{{cite journal |last=Sako |first=Shizuo |author2=Hidenobu Kirino |date=March 1980 |title=Flora of Isl. Suwanose-jima, Isls. Tokara, Ryukyus |journal=Bulletin of the Kagoshima University Forest |volume=8 |pages=19–53 |issn=0389-9454 |url=http://ir.kagoshima-u.ac.jp/bitstream/10232/931/1/KJ00000067468.pdf |accessdate=2009-02-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718170511/http://ir.kagoshima-u.ac.jp/bitstream/10232/931/1/KJ00000067468.pdf |archive-date=2011-07-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the [[Uji Islands]].<ref name=uji>{{cite journal |last=Sako |first=Shizuo |date=March 1988 |title=Flora of the Uji Isls., Kagoshima Pref., Kyushu |journal=Bulletin of the Kagoshima University Forest |volume=16 |pages=83–108 |issn=0389-9454 |url=http://ir.kagoshima-u.ac.jp/bitstream/10232/988/1/KJ00000067295.pdf |accessdate=2009-02-20 |display-authors=etal |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718170734/http://ir.kagoshima-u.ac.jp/bitstream/10232/988/1/KJ00000067295.pdf |archive-date=2011-07-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref> It occurs in association with [[overstorey]] species such as ''[[Ardisia sieboldii]]'' and ''[[Castanopsis sieboldii]]''.<ref name=FOC/>

==Cultivation==
''A. elatior'' is well known in cultivation and has a reputation for withstanding neglect, giving rise to its common name of cast-iron plant. It is tolerant of low light, low humidity, temperature fluctuation and irregular watering. It is best situated in a position away from direct sun to avoid leaf bleaching. Good drainage is also required for optimal growth and to avoid root rot.<ref name=mobot>{{cite web|title=Aspidistra elatior|work=PlantFinder|publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden|url=http://www.mobot.org/gardeninghelp/PlantFinder/plant.asp?code=B579|accessdate=2009-02-19| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20090304022939/http://www.mobot.org/gardeninghelp/PlantFinder/Plant.asp?code=B579| archivedate= 4 March 2009 | url-status= live}}</ref> Widely grown as a house plant, it can also be grown successfully outdoors in shade in temperate climates, where plants will generally cope with temperatures down to {{convert|-15|C|F|abbr=on|0}} but be killed by frosts of {{convert|-15|to|-20|C|F|abbr=on|0}} or below.<ref name=Brow13/>

The species is not seriously troubled by insects, but [[mite]]s and [[scale insect|scale]] may cause occasional problems. Its leaves and roots may be subject to browsing by hoofed mammals such as deer, as well as rodents and rabbits.<ref name=mobot/>

This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name="RHS2026">{{cite web |title=Find a plant: Aspidistra |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/search-results?form-mode=true&query=aspidistra |website=Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=18 July 2026}}</ref>

A number of [[cultivar]]s are available, including:<ref name=Brow13>{{cite journal |last1=Brown |first1=Bob |year=2013 |title=High Flying Aspidistras |journal=The Garden |volume=138 |issue=1 |pages=62–65 }}</ref>
*'Asahi' (meaning "morning sun" in Japanese) – the leaves open chocolate brown, turning green from the base upwards
*'Hoshi-zora' (meaning "starry sky" in Japanese) – large, faintly speckled leaves
*'Lennon's Song' – long narrow ends to the leaves and a central paler green stripe (discovered by an American grower of cut foliage, Robin Lennon)
*'Variegata' – with white stripes running along the length of the leaf; has also won the AGM<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/89228/Aspidistra-elatior-Variegata-(v)/Details
| title = ''Aspidistra elatior'' 'Variegata' | publisher = RHS | accessdate = 12 April 2020}}</ref> 

''A. elatior'' 'Milky Way' is properly ''[[Aspidistra lurida|A. lurida]]'' 'Ginga'.<ref name=Brow13/>
